exceptions.what: the whole of textEndLine (list-item-node.ts:179-190, moved there by #56 from list-reader.ts:308-312) - 5 mutants: `at(-1)` -> `at(+1)`, the empty-text guard -> `true`, -> `false` and `===` -> `!==`, and `Math.max` -> `Math.min`
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT, for the two reasons this line number has exactly one reader. (a) The empty-text arm is unreachable: the tokens are read from the item's own marker line, and `parseListMarker` matches no line that carries no text, so `text.at(-1)` is always a token - killing the `false` and `!==` mutants means constructing an item with no text at all. (b) The other three only move the answer EARLIER within the text's OWN span, and gapsOf uses it as the exclusive lower bound of the first block's gap: every line of that span is text, and only blanks and `+` lines are ever recorded, so no entry can sit in the difference

exceptions.what: continuationArm's cell guard (list-reader.ts:601 `previous !== undefined`) -> `true`
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT: the guard is the narrowing that lets the next conjunct read `previous.current.text` at all, so a mutant that drops it is a type error rather than a behavior. The redundant twin this row used to also cover (`previousText !== undefined`, one fact stated twice because `previousText` IS `previous?.current.text`) was deleted with the dead-branch sweep; the text is now read past the guard

exceptions.what: the nine emptied step-arm string literals (list-reader.ts:558, :572, :578, :633, :786, :799, :808, :820, :828) - `return "go"` and two `return "stop"`s -> `return ""`
